subject.title: chatCompletions: ignore request model when x-openclaw-agent-id header is present

question: Should a valid `x-openclaw-agent-id` make OpenAI-compatible HTTP requests tolerate or ignore a generic request-body `model`, instead of validating that body field as an OpenClaw agent target?
rationale: The code change is mechanically bounded, but it changes a documented public Gateway API contract and affects sibling OpenAI-compatible endpoints beyond chat completions.

options.title: Decide shared endpoint semantics first
options.body: Keep this open until Gateway owners choose one consistent precedence rule for chat completions, responses, and embeddings before implementation.

options.title: Adopt header precedence
options.body: Treat generic body `model` values as client compatibility metadata whenever a valid agent header selects the agent, then update the shared resolver, docs, and tests.

options.title: Preserve agent-first contract
options.body: Continue requiring `model` to be `openclaw`, `openclaw/default`, or an agent-target value, and document SDK integrations around those values plus `x-openclaw-model`.

options.title: Decide shared OpenAI-compatible semantics first
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose a consistent precedence rule for Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings.

recommendation.title: Decide shared endpoint semantics first
recommendation.body: Keep this open until Gateway owners choose one consistent precedence rule for chat completions, responses, and embeddings before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current agent-first contract and sibling endpoint expansion trace most directly to vincentkoc's Gateway history.
